---

sddviz embeds sdd and implements its `GraphStore` port, so one walk of a graph directory serves both
the viewer and the tool.

Package `application` documents that port as a seam an embedding host fills. The store walks
`.sdd/graph` once, builds the documents sdd needs, and hands over the snapshot sdd builds from them.
It keeps those same documents, which the snapshot exposes to nobody, and the views draw them.

One read means the viewer and sdd can never disagree about which entries exist. Read-only stops being
a convention and becomes a property of the type, because the store's write methods refuse.

Reading everything through the tool loses. It removes every risk of drift, at the price of parsing
prose for every entry the viewer shows, against a rendering that promises nothing.

Two readers over one directory lose as well. That shape needs far less code and satisfies no port.
Its failure mode is an entry that search finds and the list does not, which is the hardest kind to
notice.

Calling the `sdd` binary loses too. It keeps the integration indifferent to the Go API moving, and it
keeps a dependency on a compatible binary sitting on `PATH`.

This carries two costs. The file layout and the frontmatter parse belong to sddviz, and they follow
the port as it moves. sdd's own conformance suite for a graph store cannot run here, because it
applies a mutation and asserts the mutation landed.

Nothing follows from this on its own. It constrains work other entries commission.
